subject: Post-call recap & next steps — PortBron inference topology and SLOs
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@portbron.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Brooks <devon.b@portbron.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick call — LLM inference for customer support

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side so we're aligned before the deep technical discussion:

- Primary use case: real-time customer support summarization + context-aware suggestions for agents.
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for single-turn queries (goal); acceptable p95 up to 350ms under burst.
- Peak throughput: ~400 qps during campaign windows; sustained baseline ~80 qps.
- Model preferences: LLaMA-2 family (70B quantized preferred); open to 13B for lower-latency fallbacks.
- Session behavior: average 150 tokens output, average 60 tokens input; persistent KV cache per-session desirable.
- Compliance: SOC2 required; data residency US only for PII; we will share SOC2 report.
- Cost target: aim for ~= $0.006/response (ballpark), but willing to trade some cost for latency.

Attached telemetry snapshot and a short list of examples. Please confirm these points and flag anything you think we missed.

Attachments: portbron-poc-telemetry-snapshot.pdf

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of AI Platform
PortBron Systems
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@portbron.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick call — LLM inference for customer support

Maya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming we captured everything and outlining our immediate next steps: 

Key confirmations (as we heard them):
- Latency: p95 goal 200ms (soft), acceptable to 350ms under peak.
- Throughput: baseline ~80 qps, peaks ~400 qps.
- Model preference: 70B quantized primary, 13B fallback to hit tail-latency targets.
- Persistence: will evaluate session KV cache for hot contexts.
- Compliance/data residency: US-only for PII; we'll route PII through customer-managed VPC option if needed.

Our next steps (Hannah/Connor/Irene):
1) Connor will draft 2 topology options and a capacity sketch (dedicated GPU pool w/ burst vs hosted multi-variant routing).
2) Irene will prepare a short benching plan (sequence-length profiles, token budgets, quantization impacts).
3) I'll share a mutual action plan and a proposed slot for a technical deep-dive on Aug 20.

Deliverables before the call:
- Capacity sketch + rough cost model (Connor)
- Bench plan and data-request list so your team can share sample payloads (Irene)
- Mutual action plan document (attached)

Can you confirm availability for Friday, Aug 20 between 9–11am PT for the technical deep-dive (we'll bring an engineer and an infra architect)? Also, please send an anonymized sample of typical requests (or confirm we can use the telemetry snapshot you attached).

Attached: pb-mutual-action-plan-2026-08-18.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya@portbron.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Devon Brooks <devon.b@portbron.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: PortBron — initial topology notes (pre-deep-dive)

Maya / team — sharing quick technical notes ahead of Friday's call so we use time efficiently. These are initial hypotheses; we'll validate in the deep-dive.

Topology options (high level):
- Option A (Dedicated pool, single region):
  - Dedicated A100 80GB fleet (reserved) with autoscale to handle burst to ~500 qps.
  - Dedicated KV-cache endpoints co-located with inference to keep session p95 low.
  - Advantages: easiest to hit 200ms p95 for 70B quantized if sequence lengths are as stated.
  - Drawbacks: higher base cost, reserved capacity planning required.

- Option B (Hosted multi-variant with smart routing):
  - Primary: 70B quantized instances for quality; Fallback: 13B low-latency instances for tail requests.
  - Smart routing policy: latency-first for agent-facing queries; cost-fallback for background bulk processing.
  - Use prefix caching + partial KV reuse to lower repeated-token compute.

Capacity & rough compute estimate (very approximate):
- Baseline 80 qps * avg 150 output tokens => ~12k tokens/s.
- Peak 400 qps * 150 tokens => ~60k tokens/s.
- With quantized kernels and batched decode, expect a 70B quantized instance to handle ~80–120 qps at 150 tokens with p95 ~180–250ms depending on batch window.
- Suggest hybrid approach for cost/latency: reserved capacity sized for 120–150 qps + autoscale pool to handle bursts.

Data asks before deep-dive:
- Typical average & 95th percentile sequence lengths (input + output).
- Session stickiness: % of sessions that reuse context beyond 3 requests.
- Any heavy multi-turn flows ( > 6 turns) and examples.

I'll bring a short comparison table (70B quantized vs 13B float/quant) with expected p50/p95 and cost-per-1k-responses for the call.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Maya Patel <maya@portbron.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — PortBron inference topology and SLOs

Thanks, all — confirmed for Fri Aug 20 at 10:00am PT. Irene/Connor, appreciated the pre-call notes — exactly the framing we need. A few quick clarifications before the call:

- Average tokens are as quoted: input ~60, output ~150. 95th percentile output ~420 tokens for a small subset of long dialogs.
- Session stickiness: ~45% of sessions hit the same context 2–3 times; ~10% go into long multi-turn flows.
- We will upload a sanitized sample payload set to the Drive link you shared by EOD today.
- Attached is our internal SLO doc — it includes the CRM integration latency budget and agent UX constraints.

Requests for the deep-dive:
- Please include a tradeoff table (latency vs cost vs quality) for 70B quantized, 70B int8, and 13B float.
- Bring a proposal for KV-cache TTL and eviction given our session profiles.

Attachments: portbron-internal-slo-2026-08-20.pdf

See you Friday — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Maya
Head of AI Platform
PortBron Systems
